topic: Eye twitching: usually harmless (sleep, stress, caffeine) — when to see a doctor

youtube.title: Eyelid twitching on its own? Here's why 👁️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Eyelid jumping on its own? Usually harmless, but here's when to see a doctor.
கண் இமை தானாக துடிக்கிறதா? காரணம் இதோ.

• Eyelid twitching (myokymia) is a small eyelid muscle firing again and again; it usually settles by itself.
• Common triggers: poor sleep, stress, too much tea/coffee, long screen time, dry or tired eyes.
• Eye strain from glasses with the wrong power (or no glasses when you need them) can add to it.
• Try: 7–8 hours' sleep, less caffeine, screen breaks every 20 minutes, a warm compress on closed eyes.
• See a doctor if it lasts more than a few weeks, the eyelid closes fully, the eye is red/swollen, or other face muscles twitch.
• General education only, not a diagnosis.

gmb.text:
Eyelid twitching on its own? It's usually a small eyelid muscle firing again and again, and it normally settles by itself. Common triggers are poor sleep, stress, too much tea or coffee, long screen time and dry, tired eyes. Eye strain from the wrong glasses power can add to it.

What helps: 7–8 hours of sleep, less caffeine, regular screen breaks and a warm compress on closed eyes.

See a doctor if it lasts more than a few weeks, if the eyelid closes completely, if the eye turns red or swollen, or if other parts of the face start twitching.
